title: ALMA beneath the stars
caption: An ALMA antenna under the Milky Way, Operations Support Facility, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at ALMA, Chajnantor plateau, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: A single 12-metre antenna stands alone under the night sky, while the Milky Way stretches across the image amid a sea of stars. This antenna is one of many that make up the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array, ALMA.

It is not yet in its working place. The dish is waiting at the Operations Support Facility to be transported. ALMA's antennas are designed to be combined, and together they collect light at millimetre and submillimetre wavelengths, which lie well beyond what human eyes can see.

The scene shows a quiet moment in the life of a large observatory, with a lone antenna waiting beneath the night sky. The Milky Way above is our home galaxy seen from within, its glow built from the light of countless distant stars.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken in visible light with a camera at ALMA's Operations Support Facility. The camera settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long exposure gathers much more light than the eye, so the Milky Way looks brighter and more detailed here than in person.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.

explore: An array like ALMA works by combining signals from many antennas, so each individual dish is one part of a much larger instrument. This one is still waiting to join the rest.
alt: A single dish antenna beneath the Milky Way stretching across a star-filled sky.
